title: Model variant selection microcopy and UX hypotheses
body:
Purpose
This is a working doc: focused on the variant-selection UX inside the Model Catalog and Endpoint Create flows. Goal is to finalize microcopy, wireframe annotations, and a prioritized grooming list for implementation. Emphasis on making pinning explicit and reversible, and reducing accidental cost/latency regressions when users select model variants.

Audience
- Product designers and PMs
- Frontend engineers for Console
- Solutions engineers who demo the product
- Docs writers (to capture final microcopy)

Assumptions and constraints
- Console has existing model catalog list + details panel and endpoint creation modal. We want minimal surface changes.
- Customers can pick model family > version > variant (va/quantized/fast/accurate).
- Pinning a variant should be obvious, reversible, and show fallback behavior.
- Need clear cost/latency indicators inline to prevent surprises.

Top-level user flows (keeps separate screens for clarity)
1) Catalog list -> variant quick-compare
  - Row shows model family, current default version, and a small badge for pinned endpoints count.
  - Hover or click reveals compact inline variant chips: "gpt-redwood-1 (v1.2) — fast", "gpt-redwood-1 (v1.3) — quantized".
  - Microcopy above chips: "Quick variants: choose for latency vs quality" (alt: "Choose the variant that fits your budget and latency target").

2) Variant details flyout
  - Title: "Variant details"
  - Header line: variant name + small pill: "compat: chat / text-embedding"
  - Key stats row: median latency, tokens/sec, cost per 1k tokens (USD), and a model-quality score if available. Each stat has a tooltip icon. Tooltip copy examples: "Median latency measured at P95 with typical prompt mix."
  - CTA buttons: primary: "Use variant" (opens endpoint create modal pre-selected), secondary: "Pin variant" (opens pin dialog).
  - Microcopy for pin button hover: "Pin this variant for an endpoint to ensure consistent runtime behavior; unpin anytime."

3) Endpoint creation modal -> Variant selection step
  - Step header: "Choose model variant"
  - Two-column layout: left = variant list (radio), right = deep compare for selected variant.
  - Left column microcopy above list: "Select the model variant your endpoint will serve. You can pin now or change later from the endpoint settings."
  - Each variant row copy: name, one-line descriptor (e.g., "low-latency quantized"), cost delta (e.g., "—20% cost"), latency estimate ("~30ms p95"), and compatibility icons.
  - Inline affordance: small checkbox: "Pin this variant to the endpoint (recommended for production)". Hover tooltip: "Pinning locks the endpoint to this variant. When pinned, automated fallbacks are limited; use with rollouts for safer updates."
  - Default selection behavior: if user has existing endpoints pinned to any variant of this family, pre-select the variant that matches the most-used pinned endpoint (helps consistency).
  - Error state microcopy: if the variant isn't available in selected region: "Variant not available in selected region. Choose a different variant or change region."

4) Pin settings dialog
  - Title: "Pin variant to endpoint"
  - Short explainer: "Pin the endpoint to this exact model variant to guarantee outputs and performance. Pinned endpoints will not automatically upgrade to newer model variants."
  - Options (radio): "Pin permanently" / "Pin with automatic minor updates" / "Pin with staged rollouts". Each option has 1-line helper copy.
  - CTA: primary: "Confirm pin"; secondary: "Cancel". Danger note in red if choosing permanent: "Permanent pins require manual rollback to change model variant."

Copy alternatives to AB test
- Pin CTA text alternatives: ["Pin variant", "Lock variant", "Freeze model"] — hypothesis: "Pin" is clearer and less scary for users. Test for reduced hesitation in enablement funnel.
- Helper sentence for pin: alt A: "Pins lock your endpoint to this variant so responses stay consistent." alt B: "Pin to avoid automatic model upgrades and unexpected output changes."
- Endpoint modal header: alt variations: "Choose model variant" vs "Select runtime variant" vs "Pick model flavor". Hypothesis: Clear product language (variant vs flavor) affects dev trust.

Wireframe annotations (visual priorities)
- Emphasize cost + latency metrics visually (small colored bars) — first-time users scan these before selecting.
- Use iconography: shield icon for pin, lightning for latency, wallet for cost. Ensure icons have alt text for a11y.
- CTAs: primary action should explicitly state result ("Use variant for endpoint") not just generic "Use".
- When hovering the pin affordance, surface one-sentence examples of consequences: "Pinned endpoints will keep serving the pinned variant even after a new model is released."

Edge/error states and safeguards
- If a user tries to pin a variant that is in alpha/beta: show modal with checkbox: "I understand this variant is experimental and may be unstable." Microcopy: "Experimental variants have limited warranty and no SLA."
- If pinned variant becomes incompatible with a newer route (e.g., function calling change): show endpoint banner: "Pinned variant incompatible with new API contract. Consider using a compatible variant or create a canary."
- Rollback microcopy: "Rollback to previous pinned variant" and show recovery steps. Keep rollback one-click but require confirmation with typing the endpoint name for production endpoints.

Grooming backlog (priority / estimate / notes)
- 1) Variant list row redesign: show cost/latency chips inline (Priority: high, Est: 3d, Owner: Frontend).
- 2) Pin dialog with three options and confirmation UX (Priority: high, Est: 4d, Owner: PM + Frontend).
- 3) Tooltip content and analytics events for selected microcopy A/B test (Priority: medium, Est: 2d, Owner: Data + Analytics).
- 4) Flyout speed/quality score and icons (Priority: medium, Est: 2d, Owner: Design).
- 5) Region availability error path wording + e2e tests (Priority: low, Est: 1d, Owner: QA).
- 6) Accessibility pass: screen reader labels for icons and pin flow (Priority: medium, Est: 2d, Owner: Accessibility).

Open questions and decisions required
- What vocabulary do we standardize on: variant vs flavor vs build? (Decision owner: Product).
- Do we show explicit cost-per-1k-tokens for every variant or a relative delta only? Ops wants absolute numbers for billing clarity.
- Which pin options are supported by backend now vs we need API changes? Need Eng confirmation on "Pin with staged rollouts".
- Should pinning trigger an audit log entry and alert? (Security wants explicit logging).

Hypotheses and metrics to track
- H1: Adding explicit cost/latency badges reduces endpoint creation abandonment by 15% (track: modal abandonment rate).
- H2: Clarifying pin microcopy reduces accidental pin-unpin churn (track: pin/unpin rate in first 24h after create).
- H3: Providing a safe default (do not pin) increases production readiness but may increase incidents from silent model upgrades — monitor incidents linked to unexpected model changes.

Next steps
- Iterate on the wireframe mockups with updated iconography (Design: Marco).
- Frontend backlog ticket creation with copy variants for A/B (PM: Asha).
- Backend sync to confirm rollout types and audit log hooks (Owners: Tom + Priya).
- Prepare analytics plan to capture variant selection events, pin confirmation, and subsequent incidents (Data: Jenna).

Notes to reviewers
- This doc intentionally includes multiple copy alternatives for quick A/B experiments. Please comment with the label you prefer and any legal/security requirements we must reflect.
